## Report

`scripts/canary_bridge.py:26` does a bare `import alert_dedup`. That only resolves when
`scripts/` is already on `sys.path`. Running the affected test file on its own fails:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py -q
ERROR ...::test_every_bug_close_carries_valid_class[heartbeat-alert-_heartbeat_recovery_env]
  - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'alert_dedup'
ERROR ...::test_every_bug_close_carries_valid_class[binding-drift-alert-_drift_recovery_env]
  - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'alert_dedup'
1 passed, 2 errors
```

Reproduced on `origin/main` with the repo venv on PATH.

## Provenance — introduced today, not pre-existing

`scripts/alert_dedup.py` was ADDED by `0767c38ebb` (ticket 63e8, "route dependency
advisories by lane"). That change correctly EXTRACTED the dedup helpers out of
`canary_bridge.py` rather than duplicating them — the extraction was the right call — but it
left the consumers importing the new module by bare name.

## Why it matters even though CI is green

CI's full run passes because `tests/scripts/test_alert_dedup.py` inserts `scripts/` on
`sys.path` at import time, and that side effect leaks into every later-collected module in
the same session. The failure only appears when the file is run as a SUBSET — which is what
developers and agents do constantly while iterating. A test that passes in CI and fails when
you run it directly trains people to distrust the suite.

## Chosen mechanism (AC2 decision, stated up front)

**An explicit `sys.path` insert of the script's own directory, immediately above the sibling
import** — the pattern already established in this repo by
`scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:46-51`. Rationale, and why the two alternatives are
rejected:

- *Package-relative import* — rejected. These modules are executed as standalone scripts by
  workflow YAML (`python scripts/canary_bridge.py heartbeat-alert …`,
  `scripts/dependency_audit.py gate`). A relative import raises
  `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` under that
  invocation, so it would trade a test-only failure for a production-canary failure.
- *Making `scripts/` a real package* — rejected. Adding `scripts/__init__.py` changes how
  every script in the directory is resolved by every existing caller (workflows, Makefile,
  pre-commit), which is a far larger blast radius than the defect, and is not
  behavior-preserving.

The chosen insert is invocation-independent: it derives the directory from `__file__`, so it
holds under `python scripts/x.py`, `python -m pytest`, bare `pytest`, and
`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` alike. It is idempotent (guarded by a membership
check) and does not reorder any path entry that is already present.

## Sweep of sibling call sites (AC3)

Every bare import under `scripts/` of a module that lives in `scripts/` or `tests/`:

| Site | Status |
|---|---|
| `scripts/canary_bridge.py:26` `import alert_dedup` | **UNGUARDED — fix here** |
| `scripts/dependency_audit.py:50` `import alert_dedup` | **UNGUARDED — fix here** |
| `scripts/calibrate_completion_floor.py:24` `from gold_set_completion import …` | SAFE — line 22 explicitly inserts `tests/unit` derived from `__file__` immediately above it |
| `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:51` `import jira_dc_field_readiness` | SAFE — lines 46-48 insert `scripts/` from `__file__`; this is the precedent pattern |
| `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:59` `from _engine_path import engine_dir` | SAFE — lines 57-58 insert `tests/` from `__file__` |

The sweep is valid as of the sha it runs against and is re-run against merged `main` before
push.

## Guard (AC4/AC5) — closing the other half of the class

Ticket `a371` (merged `1db88c92d7`) landed `tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py`, which
AST-scans for `tests.`-rooted imports **under `tests/`**. It does not look at `scripts/`, so
the class is only half-guarded. This adds the companion:
`tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py`, same AST-scan shape, asserting that every
bare import under `scripts/` naming a module that is only resolvable via a directory insert
is preceded by that insert in the same file — plus a subprocess check that the affected test
module collects when run alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — the reported repro passes standalone.**
  Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py -q` exits 0 with
  0 errors (repo venv on PATH, no wrapper).
- [ ] **AC2 — the import is resolved by an explicit, invocation-independent mechanism.** Both
  fixed sites derive the directory from `__file__` and insert it idempotently above the
  import; neither relies on ambient `sys.path` ordering.
  Verify: `python -c "import ast,sys;[sys.exit('missing insert in '+p) for p in ['scripts/canary_bridge.py','scripts/dependency_audit.py'] if '__file__' not in open(p).read().split('import alert_dedup')[0][-600:]]"` exits 0.
- [ ] **AC3 — sibling call sites swept and classified.** The table above enumerates all five
  bare sibling-import sites and states which are safe and why.
  Verify: `grep -rn "^import \|^from " scripts/*.py | grep -vE "rebar|__future__|collections|pathlib|typing|dataclasses" ` lists no bare sibling import outside the five rows above.
- [ ] **AC4 — the a371 guard has a companion covering `scripts/`.**
  Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q` exits 0, and the
  new file exists.
- [ ] **AC5 — the guard is proven RED against the defect.**
  Verify: reverting the `sys.path` insert in `scripts/canary_bridge.py` and re-running
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q` FAILS naming
  `scripts/canary_bridge.py`; restoring it makes it pass. Run this before landing and record
  the output in a ticket comment.
- [ ] **AC6 — no behavior change and no regression.**
  Verify: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit tests/scripts -q`
  all pass.

## Out of scope

Any change to what `canary_bridge.py` or `dependency_audit.py` DO — this is an import-
resolution repair only. No CLI surface, no argv, no output text changes.
